$28.8 billion. Eight months ago it was $12.7 billion.

Shield AI just more than doubled its valuation after raising $2.5 billion and announcing a $5.3 billion acquisition of radar company Echodyne. In the same week, defense AI testing company Nominal tripled to a $3 billion valuation.

Defense AI is producing the fastest capital growth in the entire AI sector — and the implications extend far beyond military applications.

Shield AI's move to acquire Echodyne is vertical integration in action: owning the sensor hardware alongside the autonomy software. This is the same pattern that has defined the most durable technology companies in history — control the full stack.

The technologies being scaled in defense — autonomous systems, edge AI, real-time decisions under physical constraints — are exactly the capabilities that commercial industries will need as AI moves beyond screens and into the real world.

The talent, the engineering approaches, and eventually the products will cross over into infrastructure, logistics, energy, and manufacturing.
